decision_policy.summary: Record the unresolved check, or ready if all six checks pass. At most one check is unresolved in any scenario, so no priority order is needed.
design_rationale: Each variable corresponds to a distinct Part 107 requirement.

Scenarios contain at most one unresolved check (generation_plan.invalid_configurations excludes every pair of unresolved states), so each non-ready outcome names that check and the rules are mutually exclusive; rule order is presentational.
Real release reviews can find several open issues at once; restricting to one is a benchmark scoping choice that removes any dependence on a priority order.
Ready means only that the six scoped checks pass.

rules.explanation: The assigned pilot must hold a valid remote pilot certificate with current aeronautical knowledge.
Required controlled-airspace authorization must be present.
Visibility below three statute miles blocks the scoped operation.
Both cloud-clearance minimums must be met.
The scoped operation excludes waivers and the structure exception, so 500 feet AGL is unresolved.
The planned 110 mph maximum exceeds the 100 mph limit.
No scoped Part 107 readiness issue remains.

sources.title: Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Regulations (Part 107)
sources.locator: Operating Requirements; Pilot Certification; Airspace Authorizations
sources.excerpt: Part 107 operations require a remote pilot certificate or direct supervision; Class B, C, D and E operations need ATC authorization; the FAA summary also states the visual-line-of-sight and operating-limit requirements.

sources.title: 14 CFR § 107.65 — Aeronautical knowledge recency
sources.excerpt: A person may not exercise remote-pilot privileges unless they passed the specified test or completed applicable recurrent training within the previous 24 calendar months.

sources.title: 14 CFR § 107.41 — Operation in certain airspace
sources.excerpt: No person may operate in Class B, Class C, or Class D airspace or within the lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport unless that person has prior authorization from Air Traffic Control.

sources.title: 14 CFR § 107.51 — Operating limitations for small unmanned aircraft
sources.excerpt: Groundspeed may not exceed 87 knots; altitude generally may not exceed 400 feet above ground; visibility must be at least 3 statute miles; cloud clearance must be at least 500 feet below and 2,000 feet horizontally.
